studies.title: Effects of preoperative beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate, arginine, and glutamine supplementation on cardiac surgery: A randomized controlled trial.
studies.abstract: In older patients undergoing cardiac surgery, physical function is a critical determinant of postoperative outcomes. Beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation has been shown to promote muscle protein anabolism and inhibit catabolism, thereby preventing muscle weakness. However, its efficacy in older patients undergoing cardiac surgery remains unknown. This study aimed to examine the effects of preoperative HMB supplementation on postoperative physical function and complications in this population. In this single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial, patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for cardiac surgery were randomized to receive HMB supplementation or no nutritional intervention. The HMB group received HMB 1200 mg, l-glutamine 7000 mg, and l-arginine 7000 mg, once or twice daily, for at least 2 weeks before surgery. Evaluations were performed at baseline and before and after surgery. The primary outcome was the 6-min walking distance (6MWD) before and after surgery. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of complications, muscle mass and strength, physical performance, and length of hospital stay. Forty-four patients with a mean age of 72.5 years (women, 38 %) were randomized to the HMB (n = 22) or control (n = 22) group. Compared with the control group, the HMB group demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in the 6MWD both at the pre-surgery (448.0 ± 73.5 m vs. 375.5 ± 58.8 m; P = 0.01) and post-surgery time points (428.9 ± 76.4 m vs. 304.5 ± 52.3 m; P = 0.001). Muscle strength and physical performance also showed significant improvements in the HMB group. However, no significant difference in muscle mass was observed between the groups at any time point. The HMB group had a shorter hospital length of stay compared with that of the control group (16.1 ± 3.8 days vs. 20.4 ± 7.6 days, P = 0.03), and no adverse events were observed with the intervention. Preoperative HMB supplementation in older adults undergoing cardiac surgery resulted in significant improvements in postoperative exercise capacity and physical function, along with a reduction in the length of hospital stay, without affecting muscle mass. studies.title: Effects of multicomponent training and HMB supplementation on disability, cognitive and physical function in institutionalized older adults aged over 70 years:
studies.abstract: To investigate the synergist effects of exercise and β-hydroxy β-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation on disability, cognitive and physical function, and muscle power in institutionalized older people. Cluster-randomized controlled trial. Seventy-two institutionalized older adults (age = 83 ± 10 years old; 63% women) were randomized in four groups: exercise plus placebo (EX), HMB supplementation, EX plus HMB supplementation (EX + HMB), and control (CT). The exercising participants completed a 12-week tailored multicomponent exercise intervention (Vivifrail; 5 days/week of an individualized resistance, cardiovascular, balance and flexibility program), whereas the HMB groups received a drink containing 3 g/day of HMB. Participants were assessed Pre and Post intervention for disability and cognitive function (validated questionnaires), physical function (short physical performance battery, SPPB), handgrip strength and sit-to-stand relative muscle power. Linear mixed-effect models were used to compare changes among groups. Compared to baseline, both EX and EX + HMB improved cognitive function (+2.9 and +1.9 points; p < 0.001), SPPB score (+2.9 points and +2.4 points; p < 0.001) and relative muscle power (+0.64 and +0.48 W·kg The Vivifrail exercise program was effective in improving cognitive and physical function, and muscle power in nursing home residents, while HMB supplementation did not provide additional benefits when combined with exercise. These results emphasize the importance of physical exercise interventions in very old people as an essential basis for improving their overall health and quality of life.

studies.title: Effects of Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methylbutyrate Supplementation on Older Adults with Sarcopenia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study.
studies.abstract: Sarcopenia is recognized as a major public health concern because of its association with several adverse health events. Beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation reportedly delays the loss of muscle mass and function; however, the effect of HMB on sarcopenia remains inconclusive. We aimed to evaluate the impact of HMB intervention on muscle strength, physical performance, body compositions, and inflammatory factors in older adults with sarcopenia. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. This study included subjects aged ≥60 years with sarcopenia which were assigned to the HMB group (HMBG, n=18) and the placebo group (PG, n=16). The HMBG and PG were supplied with HMB and placebo products twice daily for 12 weeks, and both received resistance exercise training twice a week in 12 weeks. Hand grip strength was selected as the primary outcome; gait speed, five-time chair stand test, body composition and inflammatory indicators were selected as the secondary outcomes. The differences in changes from baseline between the two groups were analyzed using the analysis of covariance(ANCOVA). After the 12-week intervention, the HMBG demonstrated significantly greater improvements in handgrip strength (4.61(95%CI:2.93,6.28) kg, P<0.001), gait speed (0.11(95%CI:0.02,0.20)m/s, P=0.014), five-time chair stand test (-3.65 (95%CI:-5.72, -1.58)s, P=0.001), muscle quality (2.47(95%CI:1.15,3.80),kg.kg-1 P=0.001) and tumor necrosis factor-like weak inducer of apoptosis (-15.23(95%CI:-29.80,-0.66)pmol/mL, P=0.041) compared with the PG; no significant differences in skeletal muscle mass, skeletal muscle index, and other body composition parameters were found between the two groups. In older adults with sarcopenia, HMB significantly enhance the effect of resistance exercise training on muscle strength, physical performance, muscle quality, and reduced inflammatory factors. Therefore, HMB supplementation could be an effective treatment for sarcorpenia. The trial protocol was registered at http://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.aspx?proj=47571 as ChiCTR2000028778.

studies.title: Effects of a multilevel intervention of resistance training with or without beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate in medical ICU patients during entire hospitalisati
studies.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) is a prevalent and severe issue among ICU patients. Resistance training and beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) intervention have demonstrated the potential to enhance muscle function in patients with sarcopenia and in older adults. The purpose of this study was to determine whether resistance training and/or HMB administration would improve physical function, muscle strength, and quality of life in medical ICU patients. In this multicentre, four-arm, single-blind randomised control trial, a total of 112 adult patients with internal medical diagnoses admitted to the ICU were enrolled. These participants were then randomly assigned to one of four treatment groups: the resistance training group received protocol-based multilevel resistance exercise, the HMB group received 3 g/day of HMBCa, combination group and control groups received standard care, from the ICU to the general ward until discharge. The primary outcomes assessed at discharge included six-minute walking distance (6MWD) and short physical performance battery (SPPB). Secondary outcomes measured included muscle mass, MRC score, grip strength, and health reports quality of life at different time points. Data analysis was performed using a generalised linear mixed model, adhering to the principles of intention-to-treat analysis. Resistance training and combination treatment groups exhibited significant increases in SPPB scores (3.848 and 2.832 points, respectively) compared to the control group and substantial improvements in 6WMD (99.768 and 88.577 m, respectively) (all with P < 0.01). However, no significant changes were observed in the HMB group. Muscle strength, as indicated by MRC and grip strength tests conducted at both ICU and hospital discharge, showed statistically significant improvements in the resistance training and combination groups (P < 0.05). Nevertheless, no significant differences were found between the treatment groups and usual care in terms of 60-day mortality, prevalence of ICU-AW, muscle mass, quality of life, or other functional aspects. Resistance training with or without beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate during the entire hospitalisation intervention improves physical function and muscle strength in medical ICU patients, but muscle mass, quality of life, and 60-day mortality were unaffected. studies.title: Short-term beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate supplementation does not reduce symptoms of eccentric muscle damage.
studies.abstract: We examined the effects of short-term beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation on symptoms of muscle damage following an acute bout of eccentric exercise. Non-resistance trained subjects were randomly assigned to a HMB supplement group (HMB, 40mg/kg bodyweight/day, n = 8) or placebo group (CON, n = 9). Supplementation commenced 6 days prior to a bout of 24 maximal isokinetic eccentric contractions of the elbow flexors and continued throughout post-testing. Muscle soreness, upper arm girth, and torque measures were assessed pre-exercise, 15 min post-exercise, and 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and 10 days post-exercise. No pre-test differences between HMB and CON groups were identified, and both performed a similar amount of eccentric work during the main eccentric exercise bout (p > .05). HMB supplementation had no effect on swelling, muscle soreness, or torque following the damaging eccentric exercise bout (p > .05). Compared to a placebo condition, short-term supplementation with 40mg/kg bodyweight/day of HMB had no beneficial effect on a range of symptoms associated with eccentric muscle damage. If HMB can produce an ergogenic response, a longer preexercise supplementation period may be necessary.

studies.title: High-dose medium-term HMB supplementation did not trigger body composition changes in trained and untrained males under usual conditions or high-intensity funct
studies.abstract:
Introduction

β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation may support fat-free mass (FFM) increase and fat mass (FM) decrease. Its utility has been studied mainly for 3 gHMB·day-1 and long-term supplementation (e.g., 12 weeks). Therefore, new and personalized effective HMB supplementation protocols should be verified.

Methods

Ninety trained (TR, n = 53; 29.1 ± 7.7 years; FFM: 84.1 ± 5.1%) and untrained (UTR, n = 37; 32.3 ± 7.6 years; FFM: 75.7 ± 7.7%) males completed the randomized parallel-group placebo (PLA)-controlled study aiming at evaluating the influence of new individualized high-dose mid-term liquid HMB free acid supplementation protocol (90 mgHMB·kgFFM -1·day-1) alone (3 weeks; first period) and combined with high-intensity functional training (HIFT; 3 weeks; second period) on body mass (BM), FFM and FM, and total body water (TBW). The Fight Gone Bad (FGB) workout was an additional HIFT stimuli (2 units·week-1). Testing was performed at baseline (BAS) and after the first (SUP) and the second (SUP+FGB) study periods.

Results

HMB doses were 4.8-7.8 gHMB·day-1. The intervention had no significant effect on BM, FFM, FM, or TBW. BM, FFM (kg), TBW, and TBW/FFM were higher at SUP+FGB vs. BAS regardless of the implemented treatment and training status. Nevertheless, there was an impact (p < 0.05) from training status (but not HMB/PLA) on FM (kg; slight increases in UTR) and TBW (slight decreases in UTR).

Discussion

The individually adjusted high HMB dose did not change body mass and composition in trained or untrained individuals during a three-week exclusive supplementation or three-week supplementation in combination with additional HIFT stimuli. Therefore, any modifications in this area may likely require a longer treatment period.

studies.title: Characterisation of equine satellite cell transcriptomic profile response to β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB).
studies.abstract: β-Hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB) is a popular ergogenic aid used by human athletes and as a supplement to sport horses, because of its ability to aid muscle recovery, improve performance and body composition. Recent findings suggest that HMB may stimulate satellite cells and affect expressions of genes regulating skeletal muscle cell growth. Despite the scientific data showing benefits of HMB supplementation in horses, no previous study has explained the mechanism of action of HMB in this species. The aim of this study was to reveal the molecular background of HMB action on equine skeletal muscle by investigating the transcriptomic profile changes induced by HMB in equine satellite cells in vitro. Upon isolation from the semitendinosus muscle, equine satellite cells were cultured until the 2nd day of differentiation. Differentiating cells were incubated with HMB for 24 h. Total cellular RNA was isolated, amplified, labelled and hybridised to microarray slides. Microarray data validation was performed with real-time quantitative PCR. HMB induced differential expressions of 361 genes. Functional analysis revealed that the main biological processes influenced by HMB in equine satellite cells were related to muscle organ development, protein metabolism, energy homoeostasis and lipid metabolism. In conclusion, this study demonstrated for the first time that HMB has the potential to influence equine satellite cells by controlling global gene expression. Genes and biological processes targeted by HMB in equine satellite cells may support HMB utility in improving growth and regeneration of equine skeletal muscle; however, the overall role of HMB in horses remains equivocal and requires further proteomic, biochemical and pharmacokinetic studies.

studies.title: Resistance training and β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate for functional recovery in critical illness: a multicenter 2 × 2 factorial randomized trial.

studies.title: Evaluation of the recovery after heart surgery following preoperative supplementation with a combination of beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate, L-arginine, and L-
studies.abstract: The preoperative period is a good time to improve nutrition status, compensate for nutrient deficiencies, and optimize immune function in patients' underlying surgery. In some medical conditions, supplementation with a combination of L-glutamine (Gln), β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), and L-arginine (Arg) had promising effects on improving recovery. The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of supplementation with Gln/Arg/HMB in patients undergoing heart surgery. This randomized clinical trial was conducted on 70 patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Participants were requested to consume 2 sachets of a combination of 7 g L-arginine, 7 g L-glutamine, and 1.5 g daily HMB or placebo 30 days before operation. At the baseline and end of the study, left ventricular ejection fraction and the serum levels of troponin, creatine phosphokinase (CPK), CPK-MB, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and bilirubin were measured. Also, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, time of stay in hospital and intensive care unit (ICU), and postoperative complications were recorded after surgery. In total, 60 preoperative patients (30 in each group) with a mean age of 53.13 ± 14.35 years completed the study (attrition rate = 85.7%). Subjects in the Gln/Arg/HMB group had lower serum levels of CPK-MB (median [IQR] = 49 [39.75] vs. 83 [64.55]; P = 0.011), troponin (median [IQR] = 2.13 [1.89] vs. 4.34 [1.99]; P < 0.001), bilirubin (median [IQR] = 0.50 [0.20] vs. 0.40 [0.22]; P < 0.001), and SOFA score (median [IQR] = 2 [2] vs. 5 [2]; P < 0.001) at end of the study compared to the placebo. Also, the time of stay in the hospital (median [IQR] = 5 [1] vs. 6 [3]; P < 0.001) and ICU (median [IQR] = 2.50 [1.00] vs. 3.50 [1.50]; P = 0.002) was lower in the Gln/Arg/HMB group. The present study showed that perioperative supplementation with a combination of Gln, Arg, and HMB enhances the recovery, reduces myocardial injury, and decreases the time of hospital and ICU stay in cardiac surgery patients. These results need to be confirmed in a larger trial. IRCT.ir IRCT20120913010826N31. Registered on 13 October 2020.

studies.title: Effect of administration of β-hydroxy-β-methyl butyrate-enriched formula after liver transplantation: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
studies.abstract: Most patients undergoing liver transplantation (LT) have decreased skeletal muscle mass, malnutrition, and decreased physical activity levels. These comorbidities may prevent early recovery after surgery. The aim of this study was to examine the effects of oral nutritional formula-enriched β-hydroxy-β-methyl-butyrate (HMB), a leucine metabolite that promotes muscle synthesis and suppresses proteolysis, on postoperative sarcopenia and other outcomes after adult-to-adult living donor LT (LDLT). Thirty-three consecutive patients who underwent adult LDLT between March 2017 and October 2018 and who met inclusion criteria were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the HMB or control group. Patients in the HMB group received two packs of HMB-rich nutrients per day, which contained calcium-HMB (1500 mg), l-arginine (7000 mg), and l -glutamine (7000 mg) per pack orally or enterally from postoperative day 1 to 30 with postoperative rehabilitation. The primary endpoint was grip strength (GS) at 2 mo after LDLT. Secondary endpoints included GS at 1 mo after LDLT, skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) at 1 and 2 mo after LDLT, laboratory findings, incidence of postoperative bacteremia, and postoperative hospital length of stay (LOS). Twelve patients in the HMB group and 11 in the control group were included in the final analysis. GS at 1 and 2 mo and SMI values at 2 mo were significantly higher in the HMB group than in the control group (GS: both P < 0.001, SMI: P = 0.04). In the HMB group, white blood cell count 3 wk after LDLT was significantly lower (P = 0.005), and postoperative hospital LOS was significantly shorter (P = 0.028) compared with the control group. The incidence of postoperative bacteremia was lower in the HMB group. Postoperative administration of HMB-enriched formula with rehabilitation significantly increased GS at 1 and 2 mo and SMI at 2 mo and shortened postoperative hospital LOS after LDLT.

studies.title: Two and Four Weeks of β-Hydroxy-β-Methylbutyrate (HMB) Supplementations Reduce Muscle Damage Following Eccentric Contractions.
studies.abstract: This study investigated the effect of β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation for either 2 or 4 weeks on the muscle damage after elbow flexors after eccentric contractions (ECCs). Twenty-eight untrained men were completed the double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel design study. The subjects were randomly assigned to the ingestion of HMB supplement for 2 weeks (HMB 2-week, n = 10), for 4 weeks (HMB 4-week, n = 10), or a placebo group (PL, n = 8). Subjects of HMB 2-week and HMB 4-week consumed 3 g HMB per day, and they performed 6 sets of 10 ECCs at 100% maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) using a dumbbell. Changes in MVC torque, range of motion (ROM), upper arm circumference, muscle soreness, and muscle stiffness were assessed before, immediately after, and 1, 2, and 5 days after exercise. MVC torque and ROM were significantly higher in the HMB 2-week and HMB 4-week groups than in the PL group after ECCs (p < 0.05). The upper arm circumference was significantly smaller in the HMB 2- and 4-week groups than in the PL group after ECCs (p < 0.05). In addition, muscle stiffness at 150° was significantly lower in the HMB 2- and 4-week groups than in the PL group at immediately after ECCs (p < 0.05). However, there was no difference in all outcomes between HMB 2-week and HMB 4-week. We concluded that more than 2 weeks of HMB supplementation has a positive role for untrained subjects to prevent the muscle damage after ECCs.

studies.title: β-Hydroxy β-Methylbutyrate (HMB) Supplementation Effects on Body Mass and Performance in Elite Male Rugby Union Players.

During the supplementation period, body mass increased with HMB 0.57 ± 2.60 kg but decreased with placebo 1.39 ± 2.02 kg (p = 0.029). However, on the yo-yo intermittent recovery test (YoYo IR-1), the placebo group improved 4.0 ± 2.8 levels but HMB decreased 2.0 ± 3.0 levels (p = 0.003). studies.title: Effectiveness of nutritional supplementation on sarcopenia and recovery in hip fracture patients. A multi-centre randomized trial.
studies.abstract: Functional deterioration and reduced mobility in elderly patients with a hip fracture are associated with a loss of both muscle mass and function (sarcopenia). The aim of this study was to assess whether oral nutritional supplementation (ONS) improves muscle mass and nutritional markers (BMI, proteins) in elderly patients with hip fracture. Patients aged 65 years and over with hip fractures admitted to either of two rehabilitation facilities were included. Patients with diabetes, with Barthel index scores <40 prior to the fracture or with pathological fractures were excluded. A random-numbers generator was used to randomly allocate patients to the intervention group (IG) or the control group (CG). Those in the IG received a standard diet plus ONS in the form of two bottles a day of β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), while those in the CG received a standard diet only. The intervention was not blinded. In order to assess changes in body mass index (BMI), anthropometric parameters were recorded at both admission and discharge. Patients' functional situation was evaluated using the Barthel index (BI) and the Functional Ambulation Categories (FAC) score. Muscle mass was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, which allowed us to calculate appendicular lean mass (aLM). The outcome variable was the difference between aLM upon discharge, minus aLM upon admission (Δ-aLM). Of the 107 randomised patients (IG n55, CG n52), 49 finished the study in the IG and 43 in the CG. BMI and aLM were stable in IG patients, whilst these parametres decreased in the CG. A significant difference was observed between the two groups (p<0.001, and p=0.020 respectively). The predictive factors for Δ-aLM were ONS (p=0.006), FAC prior to fracture (p<0.001) and BI prior to fracture (p=0.007). The concentration of proteins (p=0.007) and vitamin D (p.001) had increased more in the IG than in the CG. A diet enriched in HMB improves muscle mass, prevents the onset of sarcopenia and is associated with functional improvement in elderly patients with hip fractures. Orally administered nutritional supplements can help to prevent the onset of sarcopenic obesity. www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT01404195, registered 22 July 2011, HYPERPROT-GER Study.

studies.title: The Effect of a 12-Week Beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) Supplementation on Highly-Trained Combat Sports Athletes: A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Con

studies.title: The Effect of β-Hydroxy-β-Methylbutyrate on Aerobic Capacity and Body Composition in Trained Athletes.
studies.abstract: Durkalec-Michalski, K and Jeszka, J. The effect of β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate on aerobic capacity and body composition in trained athletes. J Strength Cond Res 30(9): 2617-2626, 2016-The aim of this study was to investigate whether supplementation with β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB) affects body composition, aerobic capacity, or intramuscular enzymes activity, as well as in anabolic and/or catabolic hormones and lactate concentrations. A cohort of 58 highly trained males was subjected to 12-week supplementation with HMB (3 × 1 gHMB·d) and a placebo (PLA) in randomized, PLA controlled, double-blind crossover trials, with a 10-day washout period. Body composition and aerobic capacity were recorded, whereas the levels of creatine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase, testosterone, cortisol, and lactate, as well as the T/C ratio, in blood samples were measured. After HMB supplementation, fat-free mass increased (+0.2 kgHMB vs. -1.0 kgPLA, p = 0.021), with a simultaneous reduction of fat mass (-0.8 kgHMB vs. +0.8 kgPLA, p < 0.001). In turn, after HMB supplementation, in comparison to PLA, maximal oxygen uptake (V[Combining Dot Above][Combining Dot Above]O2max: +0.102 L·minHMB vs. -0.063 L·minPLA, p = 0.013), time to reach ventilatory threshold (VT) (TVT: +1.0 minHMB vs. -0.4 minPLA, p < 0.0001), threshold load at VT (WVT: +20 WHMB vs. -7 WPLA, p = 0.001), and the threshold heart rate at VT (HRVT: +8 b·minHMB vs. -1 b·minPLA, p < 0.0001) increased significantly. Analysis of the tested biochemical markers shows significant differences only in relation to the initial concentration. In HMB group, testosterone levels increased (p = 0.047) and in both groups (HMB: p = 0.008; PLA: p = 0.008) higher cortisol levels were observed. The results indicate that supplying HMB promotes advantageous changes in body composition and stimulates an increase in aerobic capacity, although seeming not to significantly affect the levels of the analyzed blood markers.

studies.title: Short-term beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate supplementation does not reduce symptoms of eccentric muscle damage.
studies.abstract: We examined the effects of short-term beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation on symptoms of muscle damage following an acute bout of eccentric exercise. Non-resistance trained subjects were randomly assigned to a HMB supplement group (HMB, 40mg/kg bodyweight/day, n = 8) or placebo group (CON, n = 9). Supplementation commenced 6 days prior to a bout of 24 maximal isokinetic eccentric contractions of the elbow flexors and continued throughout post-testing. Muscle soreness, upper arm girth, and torque measures were assessed pre-exercise, 15 min post-exercise, and 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and 10 days post-exercise. No pre-test differences between HMB and CON groups were identified, and both performed a similar amount of eccentric work during the main eccentric exercise bout (p > .05). HMB supplementation had no effect on swelling, muscle soreness, or torque following the damaging eccentric exercise bout (p > .05). Compared to a placebo condition, short-term supplementation with 40mg/kg bodyweight/day of HMB had no beneficial effect on a range of symptoms associated with eccentric muscle damage. If HMB can produce an ergogenic response, a longer preexercise supplementation period may be necessary.

studies.title: Effects of beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate on muscle damage after a prolonged run.
studies.abstract: This study examined the effects of supplemental beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) on muscle damage as a result of intense endurance exercise. Subjects (n = 13) were paired according to their 2-mile run times and past running experience. Each pair was randomly assigned a treatment of either HMB (3 g/day) or a placebo. After 6 wk of daily training and supplementation, all subjects participated in a prolonged run (20-km course). Creatine phosphokinase and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) activities were measured before and after a prolonged run to assess muscle damage. The placebo-supplemented group exhibited a significantly greater (treatment main effect, P = 0.05) increase in creatine phosphokinase activity after a prolonged run than did the HMB-supplemented group. In addition, LDH activity was significantly lower (treatment main effect, P = 0.003) with HMB supplementation compared with the placebo-supplemented group. In conclusion, supplementation with 3.0 g of HMB results in a decreased creatine phosphokinase and LDH response after a prolonged run. These findings support the hypothesis that HMB supplementation helps prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

studies.title: Efficacy of preoperative amino acid supplements on postoperative physical function and complications in open heart surgery patients: A study protocol for a rand
studies.abstract: Elderly patients undergoing cardiac surgery often show poor nutritional status, muscle wasting, and sarcopenia, which are reported to affect postoperative functional recovery and incidence of complications. Amino acids are essential in maintaining nutritional status, synthesizing muscle protein, and promoting beneficial energy balance of the heart muscle. β-Hydroxy β-methylbutyric acid (HMB) is a leucine metabolite known to increase muscle protein synthesis and inhibit protein catabolism; it has been used to more effectively support patients with muscle wasting due to wearing diseases. However, the efficacy of amino acid administration comprising HMB in patients undergoing open heart surgery remains unclear. This study aims to examine whether preoperative short-term aggressive amino acid administration helps support postoperative recovery of physical function and prevent complications. This is a single-center prospective randomized controlled trial (UMIN000030490). Patients aged ≥65 years who will be hospitalized for medical examination before cardiac surgery will be recruited. The participants will be randomly assigned to the experimental or control group. The experimental group will be administered with an amino acid supplement with HMB 1200mg, l-glutamine 7000mg, and l-arginine 7000mg once or twice per day depending on the degree of renal dysfunction, for 14-28 days preoperatively. The control group will not receive any nutritional intervention. The main outcome will be a change in the 6-min walking test distance pre- and postoperatively as a sign of functional recovery. Secondary outcomes such as the incidence of complications; physical, nutritional, and psychological states; mortality; and length of hospital stay will also be evaluated. This clinical study will determine the effects of preoperative short-term oral amino acid supplementation with HMB, l-glutamine, and l-arginine on postoperative physical function in elderly patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

studies.title: Preoperative Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methyl-Butyrate Supplementation Reduces Mitochondrial Dynamics Proteins and Preserves Hepatic Mitochondrial Function After Partia
studies.abstract: The liver exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity, enabling this organ to maintain homeostasis even after significant injury. However, hepatic regeneration requires sufficient energy to sustain cellular hypertrophy and proliferation, thus ensuring efficient tissue repair. Therefore, dietary modulation of pathways regulating mitochondrial quality may enhance liver regeneration. This study aimed to investigate the effects of preoperative beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB) supplementation on mitochondrial quality control pathways and its impact on the liver regeneration process in mice undergoing partial hepatectomy (PHx). Male C57BL/6J mice were supplemented with 600 mg/kg HMB via gavage for 10 days. On the 10th day, supplementation was discontinued, and the mice underwent a ⅔ liver resection. The subsequent 7 days have constituted the liver regeneration period. For a second injury induction, at the end of the 7th day of regeneration, acetaminophen (APAP) overdose was administered via gavage. We then analyzed several markers of mitochondrial quality and liver function. Our results indicate that preoperative HMB supplementation modulates cell cycle progression, preventing excessive hepatic mass accumulation. Additionally, HMB regulates mitochondrial dynamics by decreasing Parkin, Mfn2, and DRP1 protein levels while increasing the mitochondrial markers VDAC2 and Tom20. Following a second injury from an APAP overdose, the HMB-supplemented group demonstrated increased mtDNA content and enhanced mitochondrial capacity, both critical for effective tissue recovery. Our findings suggest that preoperative HMB supplementation preserves hepatic mitochondrial capacity after PHx.

studies.title: β-Hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate enhances fast-twitch muscle and mitochondrial function, histopathology and mTORC1 signalling in the <i>mdx</i> dystrophic
studies.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is one of the most severe forms of inheritable muscular dystrophies, caused by a genetic mutation resulting in the loss of dystrophin. Dystrophin loss initiates a cascade of negative mechanistic changes in skeletal muscle, such as disrupted protein homeostasis and mitochondrial dysfunction. Recent evidence suggests the leucine metabolite, β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), may improve physical function in DMD boys and improve aspects of the dystrophic phenotype in preclinical mdx mice. HMB has been shown to modulate protein turnover and mitochondrial function, both of which are dysregulated in DMD. Therefore, this study examined the effect of 3-wk of HMB supplementation (0.75 mg/g/day via drinking water), starting at 3-wk of age in mdx mice. HMB-treated mdx mice exhibited increased full-body grip strength and holding impulse, compared with mdx controls. HMB treatment also increased normalized muscle mass of the fast-twitch extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscle, which coincided with increased average fiber size and improved absolute/specific in vitro force production. Moreover, HMB-treated EDL muscles displayed increased mitochondrial complex II succinate dehydrogenase activity, alongside upregulated markers of mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signalling (p70S6K1 and 4EBP1 phosphorylation), suggestive of increased protein synthesis. Finally, muscle fibers isolated from HMB-treated mdx mice showed improved mitochondrial efficiency that was associated with increased maximal respiration, spare respiratory capacity, and ATP synthesis. This study is the first to show HMB-induced improvements on in vitro and in vivo measures of mdx skeletal muscle force production that are coupled with improved mitochondrial function, suggesting that HMB may be a viable treatment option for DMD.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This is the first study to examine the effect of HMB in 3-wk-old mdx mice undergoing extensive muscle damage and regeneration both in vivo and in vitro. HMB treatment increased voluntary grip strength and holding impulse, while elevating force production of isolated mdx EDL muscles, which were associated with improved muscle mass, muscle fiber size, and succinate dehydrogenase activity. Finally, these improvements coincided with increased markers of mTORC1 signalling, mitochondrial respiration, and ATP production.

studies.title: Characterisation of equine satellite cell transcriptomic profile response to β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB).
studies.abstract: β-Hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB) is a popular ergogenic aid used by human athletes and as a supplement to sport horses, because of its ability to aid muscle recovery, improve performance and body composition. Recent findings suggest that HMB may stimulate satellite cells and affect expressions of genes regulating skeletal muscle cell growth. Despite the scientific data showing benefits of HMB supplementation in horses, no previous study has explained the mechanism of action of HMB in this species. The aim of this study was to reveal the molecular background of HMB action on equine skeletal muscle by investigating the transcriptomic profile changes induced by HMB in equine satellite cells in vitro. Upon isolation from the semitendinosus muscle, equine satellite cells were cultured until the 2nd day of differentiation. Differentiating cells were incubated with HMB for 24 h. Total cellular RNA was isolated, amplified, labelled and hybridised to microarray slides. Microarray data validation was performed with real-time quantitative PCR. HMB induced differential expressions of 361 genes. Functional analysis revealed that the main biological processes influenced by HMB in equine satellite cells were related to muscle organ development, protein metabolism, energy homoeostasis and lipid metabolism. In conclusion, this study demonstrated for the first time that HMB has the potential to influence equine satellite cells by controlling global gene expression. Genes and biological processes targeted by HMB in equine satellite cells may support HMB utility in improving growth and regeneration of equine skeletal muscle; however, the overall role of HMB in horses remains equivocal and requires further proteomic, biochemical and pharmacokinetic studies.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A naturally occurring metabolite of the amino acid leucine; taken as a supplement to support muscle.
explanation.what_it_is: HMB (β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate) is a small molecule your body makes when it breaks down leucine, an amino acid found in protein. It's produced naturally in small amounts, but supplement doses deliver much larger quantities. Most people take it as a powder or capsule, typically 2–3 grams per day, usually alongside resistance training. The supplement form is synthesized in labs and is chemically identical to what your body produces.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Reduces muscle breakdown and supports muscle-building signaling, especially during resistance training.
explanation.how_it_works: HMB works via two main routes. First, it appears to reduce the breakdown of muscle proteins — your body is always both building and breaking down muscle, and HMB tips the balance toward preservation. Second, it activates signaling pathways (particularly mTOR, a cellular 'growth switch') that tell muscle cells to grow and repair themselves. This is especially powerful when you're lifting weights: resistance training creates tiny damage in muscle fibers, and HMB appears to speed and amplify the repair process. The effect is most pronounced in people doing structured strength training, and it seems to be stronger in older adults or in people recovering from illness — populations where muscle maintenance is harder.
explanation.safety_line: Well tolerated in short-term trials; long-term safety and drug interactions not well studied.
explanation.safety_detail: Randomized controlled trials spanning 2–12 weeks have reported no serious adverse events attributable to HMB supplementation across diverse populations, including older adults, post-surgical patients, and elite athletes. However, the retrieved studies are relatively short in duration and drawn from small-to-moderate cohorts, so uncommon or delayed effects remain unknown. Long-term use beyond 12 weeks is not well characterized in the records provided.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety (beyond 12 weeks) — no adequately powered trials retrieved; repeated dosing over months or years is untested.
Drug interactions — no studies retrieved examining HMB with common medications; potential interactions unknown.
Excluded populations — pregnant/nursing individuals, children, and those with severe renal or hepatic disease were largely absent from trials; safety in these groups is unestablished.
explanation.chem_meaning: HMB is a small, water-soluble organic acid (~104 Da), so it is easily absorbed from the gut and distributes throughout the body without special transport mechanisms. Its small size and polarity mean it can cross cell membranes readily and reach muscle tissue efficiently, which likely explains why oral dosing is practical and effective.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Six independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews consistently found that HMB supplementation increases muscle mass in people doing resistance training. A 2026 meta-analysis of 561 participants in older adults showed significant gains in lean body mass when HMB was paired with strength training. A 2025 systematic review of 359 patients with sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) confirmed the effect. Benefits appeared most pronounced in older adults and in people recovering from illness or surgery, though gains were observed across multiple age groups and training contexts.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: The convergence of 6 independent meta-analyses on the same outcome, plus adequately large participant numbers, provides strong confidence. The effect is replicated across diverse populations and study designs.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seven independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews found that HMB supplementation significantly improves muscle strength in people engaging in resistance training. A 2026 meta-analysis combining strength training, whey protein, and HMB in 472 older adults documented meaningful gains in strength. A 2024 meta-analysis of 279 participants examined HMB's effects on endurance performance and found benefits. Across 17 studies with disclosed sample sizes, at least 2,264 participants were tracked, though the true total is substantially larger because most abstracts do not report their cohort size.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Seven independent meta-analyses all converge on this outcome, indicating robust replication. The pooled evidence spans thousands of participants across multiple study types and populations, meeting the threshold for strong confidence.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seven independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews found that HMB supplementation improves exercise performance in healthy and at-risk populations. A pooled effect size of 0.58 (95% CI 0.28–0.87) indicates a moderate-to-small practical benefit across 20 studies (19 in humans, 1 in animals). A 2026 meta-analysis of 472 older people and a 2024 meta-analysis of 279 participants in endurance settings both documented improvements in work capacity, fatigue resistance, and task completion.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Seven independent meta-analyses all report consistent findings, with a pooled quantitative effect and a moderate confidence interval, establishing strong evidence for the effect.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Twelve human and three animal studies examined HMB's effects on muscle recovery and soreness following exercise or surgery. A 2026 RCT in elite judokas found HMB reduced markers of muscle damage and improved antioxidant status after acute exercise. A 2025 RCT of 134 patients in critical illness showed faster functional recovery with HMB plus resistance training. A 2019 RCT of 10 participants found two to four weeks of HMB reduced muscle damage from eccentric exercise. Across five studies with disclosed sample sizes, at least 241 participants were included, though the true total is larger. However, no pooled meta-analysis confirmed that all available studies agree on the magnitude of the effect.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: While multiple well-designed trials report consistent benefits for recovery markers, inconsistency in outcomes across studies and the absence of a completed meta-analysis prevent a 'Strong' grade. The evidence is sufficient to indicate an effect, but the boundaries of efficacy are less clear than for muscle growth and strength.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base is predominantly human (73 human studies vs. 24 animal studies across all outcomes). The records include 6–7 independent meta-analyses per outcome conducted between 2024–2026, representing high-quality synthesis of randomized controlled trials and some observational studies. Median sample sizes in disclosed trials range from 70–712 participants, and pooled participant numbers exceed 2,000 for muscle strength and growth. The literature is recent and active, with most data from 2022 onward, suggesting confidence in contemporary evidence while acknowledging that longer-term follow-up studies (beyond 12 weeks) remain limited.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records do not clearly delineate whether HMB's benefits extend equally to all populations — older adults and post-surgical patients appear heavily represented, while studies in young, healthy athletes are less prominent. Most trials span 8–12 weeks; whether gains persist or grow with supplementation beyond 3 months is not addressed in the provided abstracts. Finally, the recovery/soreness outcome lacks a quantitative meta-analysis, leaving open whether the effect is consistent and clinically meaningful across diverse exercise and surgical settings.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un metabolito que se produce naturalmente del aminoácido leucina; se toma como suplemento para apoyar la musculatura.
explanation_es.what_it_is: HMB (β-hidroxi-β-metilbutirato) es una pequeña molécula que tu cuerpo produce cuando descompone la leucina, un aminoácido que se encuentra en las proteínas. Se produce naturalmente en pequeñas cantidades, pero las dosis de suplementos suministran cantidades mucho mayores. La mayoría de las personas la toman en polvo o cápsula, típicamente 2–3 gramos por día, generalmente junto con entrenamiento de resistencia. La forma de suplemento se sintetiza en laboratorios y es químicamente idéntica a la que tu cuerpo produce.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Reduce la descomposición muscular y apoya la señalización de construcción muscular, especialmente durante el entrenamiento de resistencia.
explanation_es.how_it_works: HMB funciona a través de dos rutas principales. En primer lugar, parece reducir la descomposición de proteínas musculares — tu cuerpo siempre está tanto construyendo como descomponiendo músculo, y HMB inclina el balance hacia la preservación. En segundo lugar, activa vías de señalización (particularmente mTOR, un 'interruptor de crecimiento' celular) que le dicen a las células musculares que crezcan y se reparen a sí mismas. Esto es especialmente poderoso cuando estás levantando pesas: el entrenamiento de resistencia crea un daño minúsculo en las fibras musculares, y HMB parece acelificar y amplificar el proceso de reparación. El efecto es más pronunciado en personas que hacen entrenamiento de fuerza estructurado, y parece ser más fuerte en adultos mayores o en personas que se recuperan de enfermedad — poblaciones donde el mantenimiento muscular es más difícil.
explanation_es.safety_line: Bien tolerado en ensayos a corto plazo; la seguridad a largo plazo y las interacciones farmacológicas no están bien estudiadas.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos controlados aleatorios que abarcan 2–12 semanas no han reportado eventos adversos graves atribuibles a la suplementación con HMB en poblaciones diversas, incluyendo adultos mayores, pacientes post-quirúrgicos y atletas de élite. Sin embargo, los estudios recuperados tienen una duración relativamente corta y provienen de cohortes pequeñas a moderadas, por lo que los efectos infrecuentes o retrasados siguen siendo desconocidos. El uso a largo plazo más allá de 12 semanas no está bien caracterizado en los registros proporcionados.
safety_bullets: Seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de 12 semanas) — no se recuperaron ensayos adecuadamente potenciados; la dosificación repetida durante meses o años no ha sido probada.
Interacciones farmacológicas — no se recuperaron estudios que examinen HMB con medicamentos comunes; las posibles interacciones son desconocidas.

Poblaciones excluidas — individuos embarazadas/lactantes, niños y aquellos con enfermedad renal o hepática grave estuvieron en gran medida ausentes de los ensayos; la seguridad en estos grupos no está establecida.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: HMB es un ácido orgánico pequeño y soluble en agua (~104 Da), por lo que se absorbe fácilmente desde el intestino y se distribuye por todo el cuerpo sin mecanismos de transporte especiales. Su pequeño tamaño y polaridad significan que puede cruzar las membranas celulares fácilmente y llegar al tejido muscular de manera eficiente, lo que probablemente explica por qué la dosificación oral es práctica y efectiva.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seis metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas encontraron consistentemente que la suplementación con HMB aumenta la masa muscular en personas que realizan entrenamiento de resistencia. Un metanálisis de 2026 de 561 participantes en adultos mayores mostró ganancias significativas en masa corporal magra cuando HMB se combinó con entrenamiento de fuerza. Una revisión sistemática de 2025 de 359 pacientes con sarcopenia (pérdida muscular relacionada con la edad) confirmó el efecto. Los beneficios parecieron más pronunciados en adultos mayores y en personas que se recuperaban de enfermedad o cirugía, aunque se observaron ganancias en múltiples grupos de edad y contextos de entrenamiento.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La convergencia de 6 metanálisis independientes en el mismo resultado, más números de participantes adecuadamente grandes, proporciona una confianza fuerte. El efecto se replica en poblaciones y diseños de estudios diversos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Siete metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas encontraron que la suplementación con HMB mejora significativamente la fuerza muscular en personas que se dedican al entrenamiento de resistencia. Un metanálisis de 2026 que combinó entrenamiento de fuerza, proteína de suero y HMB en 472 adultos mayores documentó ganancias significativas en fuerza. Un metanálisis de 2024 de 279 participantes examinó los efectos de HMB en el rendimiento de resistencia y encontró beneficios. En 17 estudios con tamaños de muestra revelados, al menos 2,264 participantes fueron seguidos, aunque el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor porque la mayoría de los resúmenes no reportan su tamaño de cohorte.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Siete metanálisis independientes todos convergen en este resultado, indicando replicación robusta. La evidencia combinada abarca miles de participantes en múltiples tipos de estudios y poblaciones, cumpliendo el umbral para una confianza fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Siete metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas encontraron que la suplementación con HMB mejora el rendimiento del ejercicio en poblaciones sanas y en riesgo. Un tamaño de efecto combinado de 0.58 (IC 95% 0.28–0.87) indica un beneficio práctico moderado a pequeño en 20 estudios (19 en humanos, 1 en animales). Un metanálisis de 2026 de 472 personas mayores y un metanálisis de 2024 de 279 participantes en contextos de resistencia ambos documentaron mejoras en capacidad de trabajo, resistencia a la fatiga y finalización de tareas.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Siete metanálisis independientes todos reportan hallazgos consistentes, con un efecto cuantitativo combinado e un intervalo de confianza moderado, estableciendo evidencia fuerte para el efecto.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Doce estudios en humanos y tres en animales examinaron los efectos de HMB en la recuperación muscular y el dolor muscular después del ejercicio o cirugía. Un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2026 en judokas de élite encontró que HMB redujo los marcadores de daño muscular y mejoró el estado antioxidante después del ejercicio agudo. Un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2025 de 134 pacientes en enfermedad crítica mostró recuperación funcional más rápida con HMB más entrenamiento de resistencia. Un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2019 de 10 participantes encontró que dos a cuatro semanas de HMB redujeron el daño muscular del ejercicio excéntrico. En cinco estudios con tamaños de muestra revelados, al menos 241 participantes fueron incluidos, aunque el total verdadero es mayor. Sin embargo, ningún metanálisis combinado confirmó que todos los estudios disponibles estén de acuerdo en la magnitud del efecto.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Aunque múltiples ensayos bien diseñados reportan beneficios consistentes para marcadores de recuperación, la inconsistencia en los resultados entre estudios y la ausencia de un metanálisis completado evitan una clasificación 'Fuerte'. La evidencia es suficiente para indicar un efecto, pero los límites de eficacia son menos claros que para el crecimiento muscular y la fuerza.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia es predominantemente en humanos (73 estudios en humanos vs. 24 estudios en animales en todos los resultados). Los registros incluyen 6–7 metanálisis independientes por resultado realizados entre 2024–2026, representando una síntesis de alta calidad de ensayos controlados aleatorios y algunos estudios observacionales. Los tamaños de muestra medianos en ensayos con datos revelados van de 70–712 participantes, y los números de participantes combinados superan 2,000 para fuerza muscular y crecimiento. La literatura es reciente y activa, con la mayoría de datos de 2022 en adelante, sugiriendo confianza en la evidencia contemporánea mientras se reconoce que los estudios de seguimiento a más largo plazo (más allá de 12 semanas) siguen siendo limitados.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados no delinean claramente si los beneficios de HMB se extienden equitativamente a todas las poblaciones — los adultos mayores y los pacientes post-quirúrgicos parecen estar fuertemente representados, mientras que los estudios en atletas jóvenes y sanos son menos prominentes. La mayoría de los ensayos abarcan 8–12 semanas; si las ganancias persisten o crecen con la suplementación más allá de 3 meses no se aborda en los resúmenes proporcionados. Finalmente, el resultado de recuperación/dolor muscular carece de un metanálisis cuantitativo, dejando abierto si el efecto es consistente y clínicamente significativo en contextos diversos de ejercicio y cirugía.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base is genuinely solid for muscle growth and strength in older/sarcopenic populations, with 7 convergent meta-analyses per outcome, but generalizability to healthy young adults and the mechanism linking HMB to outcomes remain underexamined.

concerns.issue: Heavy concentration in sarcopenia/older adult populations
concerns.detail: Five of seven meta-analyses explicitly focus on older adults or sarcopenia (2025, 2025, 2026 titles all mention 'older adults' or 'sarcopenia'). The 2024 meta-analysis on 'Endurance Performance in a Healthy Population' is labeled as such precisely because it stands apart. The evidence base does not transparently separate efficacy in healthy young exercisers from efficacy in disease/age-related muscle loss, conflating two distinct clinical questions.

For muscle growth and strength outcomes, the median sample size across reported trials is 43 and 22 respectively—far below conventional adequacy for detecting small-to-medium effects. Six of the most recent RCTs (2026, 2026, 2026, 2025, 2020, 2019) reported n≤70, with three at n≤21. The strength of the overall grade rests almost entirely on meta-analyses that pool these small trials, not on any single well-powered study. A single large trial showing null effect could materially shift the pooled result.

concerns.issue: Confounding via combined interventions masks independent effect
concerns.detail: Multiple recent RCTs combine HMB with other agents (2026: 'Combined creatine and HMB co-supplementation'; 2026: 'Combined creatine and HMB'; 2026: 'prebiotics and HMB'; 2022: 'strength training, whey protein, and HMB'). These designs cannot isolate HMB's independent contribution. The meta-analyses synthesizing these trials do not appear to stratify by intervention type, so the pooled effect may conflate HMB with creatine, protein, or training synergy.

concerns.issue: Recovery/soreness evidence remains unintegrated and inconsistent
concerns.detail: The engine explicitly notes 'Inconsistency: several studies exist but no pooled analysis confirms they agree' for recovery/soreness, keeping this outcome at Moderate despite 15 retrieved studies. With a median sample size of only 14 across 5 reported trials and only ~241 verified participants, the evidence base is underpowered and heterogeneous. This is the only outcome for which synthesis is absent, a red flag for genuine inconsistency rather than true consensus.

concerns.issue: No extractable pooled effect for two of three primary outcomes
concerns.detail: Muscle growth and muscle strength are graded Strong with zero pooled effect sizes provided—only narrative convergence across meta-analyses. For exercise performance, a single SMD (0.58 [0.28–0.87]) is available, but it is drawn from a 2024 meta-analysis on 'Endurance Performance in a Healthy Population' (n=279), which may not align with the broader muscle-growth/strength findings in older adults. The absence of transparent, standardized pooled estimates makes independent verification of the grade impossible.

appraisal.mechanism_check: HMB is a metabolite of leucine hypothesized to reduce proteolysis and promote mTOR signaling, a plausible pathway for muscle protein accretion. However, the records do not show whether the clinical trials directly measured these mechanisms (e.g., MPS, proteolysis markers, mTOR activation) or relied solely on distal endpoints (lean mass, strength). The leap from biochemical mechanism to clinical muscle growth is standard for this class of study, but if the trials are short-term or measure only strength (a neuromuscular output) without confirming hypertrophy, the mechanistic claim remains indirect.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that most individual RCTs are n<50 with minimal description of blinding, allocation concealment, or dropout rates in these abstracts. The meta-analyses converge by design because they repeatedly pool the same small, potentially biased trials. The inclusion of confounded multi-agent trials (HMB+creatine, HMB+protein) inflates apparent efficacy. Most critically, the application to young healthy exercisers is extrapolated from sarcopenia/older adult data; no large RCT in young athletes shows robust, independent HMB effect on muscle growth or strength.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A large (n≥200), blinded RCT in healthy young resistance-trained adults, with HMB-only versus placebo, measuring lean mass via DEXA/MRI and strength via 1RM over 12+ weeks, would clarify whether the effect generalizes beyond older/sarcopenic populations and exists independent of confounders. Alternatively, a prospective meta-regression examining effect size as a function of age, training status, and co-interventions would transparently partition the dose of HMB's independent contribution.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia es genuinamente sólida para el crecimiento muscular y la fuerza en poblaciones mayores/sarcopénicas, con 7 metanálisis convergentes por resultado, pero la generalización a adultos jóvenes sanos y el mecanismo que vincula el HMB con los resultados permanecen insuficientemente examinados.

concerns.issue: Concentración pesada en poblaciones de sarcopenia/adultos mayores
concerns.detail: Cinco de siete metanálisis se enfocan explícitamente en adultos mayores o sarcopenia (los títulos de 2025, 2025, 2026 todos mencionan 'adultos mayores' o 'sarcopenia'). El metanálisis de 2024 sobre 'Desempeño en Resistencia en una Población Sana' se etiqueta como tal precisamente porque se destaca. La base de evidencia no separa de manera transparente la eficacia en ejercitadores jóvenes sanos de la eficacia en la pérdida muscular relacionada con la enfermedad/edad, confundiendo dos preguntas clínicas distintas.

concerns.issue: La mayoría de los ensayos clínicos individuales severamente insuficientemente potenciados
concerns.detail: Para resultados de crecimiento muscular y fuerza, el tamaño mediano de muestra en los ensayos reportados es 43 y 22 respectivamente, muy por debajo de la adecuación convencional para detectar efectos pequeños a medianos. Seis de los ensayos clínicos más recientes (2026, 2026, 2026, 2025, 2020, 2019) reportaron n≤70, con tres en n≤21. La solidez de la calificación general descansa casi enteramente en metanálisis que agrupan estos ensayos pequeños, no en ningún estudio único bien potenciado. Un único ensayo grande que muestre efecto nulo podría cambiar materialmente el resultado agrupado.

concerns.issue: Confusión a través de intervenciones combinadas enmascaró el efecto independiente
concerns.detail: Múltiples ensayos clínicos recientes combinan HMB con otros agentes (2026: 'Cosupplementación combinada de creatina y HMB'; 2026: 'Creatina y HMB combinados'; 2026: 'Prebióticos y HMB'; 2022: 'Entrenamiento de fuerza, proteína de suero y HMB'). Estos diseños no pueden aislar la contribución independiente del HMB. Los metanálisis que sintetizan estos ensayos no parecen estratificar por tipo de intervención, por lo que el efecto agrupado puede confundir HMB con sinergia de creatina, proteína o entrenamiento.

concerns.issue: La evidencia de recuperación/dolor muscular permanece no integrada e inconsistente
concerns.detail: El motor explícitamente nota 'Inconsistencia: existen varios estudios pero ningún análisis agrupado confirma que estén de acuerdo' para recuperación/dolor muscular, manteniendo este resultado en Moderada a pesar de 15 estudios recuperados. Con un tamaño mediano de muestra de solo 14 en 5 ensayos reportados y aproximadamente 241 participantes verificados, la base de evidencia está insuficientemente potenciada y es heterogénea. Este es el único resultado para el cual la síntesis está ausente, una bandera roja de verdadera inconsistencia en lugar de verdadero consenso.

concerns.issue: Sin efectos agrupados extraíbles para dos de tres resultados primarios
concerns.detail: El crecimiento muscular y la fuerza muscular se califican como Fuerte sin proporcionar tamaños de efecto agrupados: solo convergencia narrativa entre metanálisis. Para el desempeño del ejercicio, está disponible una única DME (0.58 [0.28–0.87]), pero se extrae de un metanálisis de 2024 sobre 'Desempeño en Resistencia en una Población Sana' (n=279), que puede no alinearse con los hallazgos más amplios de crecimiento muscular/fuerza en adultos mayores. La ausencia de estimaciones agrupadas transparentes y estandarizadas hace imposible la verificación independiente de la calificación.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El HMB es un metabolita de la leucina hipotetizado para reducir la proteólisis y promover la señalización de mTOR, una vía plausible para la acumulación de proteína muscular. Sin embargo, los registros no muestran si los ensayos clínicos midieron directamente estos mecanismos (p. ej., síntesis de proteína muscular, marcadores de proteólisis, activación de mTOR) o se basaron únicamente en puntos finales distales (masa magra, fuerza). El salto del mecanismo bioquímico al crecimiento muscular clínico es estándar para esta clase de estudio, pero si los ensayos son a corto plazo o miden solo fuerza (una salida neuromuscular) sin confirmar hipertrofia, la afirmación mecanicista permanece indirecta.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que la mayoría de los ensayos clínicos individuales tienen n<50 con descripción mínima de cegamiento, ocultamiento de asignación o tasas de abandono en estos resúmenes. Los metanálisis convergen por diseño porque agrupan repetidamente los mismos ensayos pequeños y potencialmente sesgados. La inclusión de ensayos de múltiples agentes confundidos (HMB+creatina, HMB+proteína) infla la eficacia aparente. Lo más crítico es que la aplicación a ejercitadores jóvenes sanos se extrapola de datos de sarcopenia/adultos mayores; ningún ensayo clínico grande en atletas jóvenes muestra un efecto robusto e independiente del HMB en el crecimiento muscular o la fuerza.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo clínico grande (n≥200), cegado, en adultos jóvenes entrenados en resistencia, con HMB solo versus placebo, midiendo masa magra mediante DEXA/RM y fuerza mediante 1RM durante 12+ semanas, aclararía si el efecto se generaliza más allá de poblaciones mayores/sarcopénicas y existe independientemente de confusores. Alternativamente, una metarregresión prospectiva examinando el tamaño del efecto como función de la edad, estado de entrenamiento e intervenciones concomitantes partiría de manera transparente la contribución independiente del HMB.
